text.p: Quantum Corp., citing record sales of its disk drives, reported fiscal third-quarter earnings Tuesday that were far better than analysts expected.

Quantum, the second-largest maker of computer disk drives, said it had net income of $52.4 million, or 71 cents a share, compared with a loss of $2.48 million, or 5 cents, in the same quarter a year ago.
The profit easily surpassed the 52 cents Wall Street was expecting, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.
Revenue for the quarter ended Dec. 29 rose 22 percent to $1.48 billion from $1.23 billion a year ago.

"Along with our record sales, we achieved record unit shipments of more than 6.6 million drives, generated over $299 million in cash from operations during the quarter and significantly reduced the loss from our high-end disk drive business," said Michael Brown, Quantum chief executive.
During the quarter, Quantum increased cash and investments to $219.3 million from $164.8 million a year ago, the company said. Meanwhile, inventory fell $106 million to $253 million.
The only disappointment, Brown said, was that the company did not make progress in reducing the loss in its business of making record heads, one of the components of disk drives.
For the recent nine months, Quantum had net income of $60.9 million, or 91 cents a share, compared with net income of $32.5 million, or 59 cents, in the same period a year ago.
Nine-month revenue rose 18 percent to $3.76 billion from $3.19 billion.
